title: Electric fields
target: Use field arrows to predict the force on a test charge.
criteria: Draw electric field arrows for isolated positive and negative charges.
Distinguish the field from a particular test charge’s force.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: At a point directly above an isolated positive source charge, which way does the electric field point?
options: Nowhere unless a test charge is present.
cpa.guide: The field of a positive source points radially outward.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A field arrow at a point to the left of an isolated negative source points right. Is that consistent?
options: No; every field arrow points left.
Yes; the arrow points toward the negative source.
No; negative sources have outward arrows.
Yes, because fields show electron velocity.
cpa.guide: The arrow describes force on a positive test charge, toward a negative source.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A field points west. A small negative test charge is placed there. Which way is its electric force?
options: Zero solely because the charge is negative.
cpa.guide: F = qE; a negative q reverses force direction relative to the field.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A positive 0.50 C model test charge experiences 3.0 N north. What is the field?
cpa.guide: E = F/q = 3.0/0.50 = 6.0 N/C; positive charge gives the same direction.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: The source charges stay fixed. A tiny positive test charge is replaced by one with twice the charge. Ignoring its effect on the source, what changes?
options: Force doubles; the source field is unchanged.
cpa.guide: E is set by the source configuration; F = qE scales with test charge.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A model field is 12 N/C downward. Which test charge would feel a 6 N upward force?
cpa.guide: Magnitude |q| = 6/12 = 0.50 C. Opposite force and field directions require negative charge.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.
